corrections.issue: Wrong speaker: this passage is the host (Graham chief client officer) summarising the systematic side, not Pablo Calderini; the transcript says pure trend is price-driven and the quant macro strategy brings in fundamental data points.
corrections.fix: The host (chief client officer) says Graham's pure trend following is price-driven while the quant macro strategy adds fundamental data to the price signal, so its positioning can evolve more dynamically.

corrections.issue: Overstated: the 'five cycles' are four completed cycles (1994-95, 1999-2000, 2005-06, 2015-18) plus the still-running 2022-23 cycle; only the four completed cycles ended in turmoil, and the 2015-18 cycle ended with turmoil in 2018 while the cut came in March 2020 with covid.
corrections.fix: In the four completed hiking cycles since Volcker (1994-95 +300bp, 1999-2000 +170-175bp, 2005-06 +425bp, 2015-18) the Fed stopped after turmoil (tequila and Asian crises, Nasdaq collapse, the global financial crisis, 2018 market turmoil); the current cycle is a fifth, still running.

completeness_estimate: 0.86 - first reader captured nearly every argument of the slide-by-slide talk (hiking cycles, core inflation, stock-bond correlation, long-horizon variance, macro skew); missed a few supporting causal links and operating details (inflation drives correlation, Fed guidance blamed, concentrated multi-PM book, recency bias).
